task: Fix the API response truncation after the response buffer size was reduced.

candidate_memories.content: API responses over 4MB are being truncated to 4MB after the response buffer size was reduced in the last deploy.
The API gateway response buffer must be restored to 16MB; it was reduced to 4MB by an accidental config change.
The buffer size was changed in the Nginx config file during an unrelated disk space optimization.
Only bulk export endpoints return responses over 4MB; all other endpoints are within the 4MB limit.
Session 3 note: the data team reported bulk export responses being truncated at exactly 4MB, corrupting the output.
Nginx is used as the API gateway with custom response buffering configuration.
Session 4 note: the platform team upgraded Nginx from 1.24 to 1.25 for HTTP/3 support.
Old practice: response buffering was disabled in the early API design for streaming responses.
The Nginx config is managed by Ansible and deployed with the infrastructure pipeline.
Session 9 note: the DevOps team added a config drift detection job for Nginx settings.
Old Nginx guide: the 4MB buffer size was the original default before large export responses were added.
API gateway buffer sizes must be set to accommodate the maximum expected response size plus a safety margin.
Session 6 note: the API team added pagination to reduce large response sizes for most endpoints.
Bulk export endpoints are rate-limited to 10 requests per minute per user to limit load.
A response size test in session 12 confirmed all standard endpoints return responses under 1MB.
The load balancer upstream buffer is set to 32MB; truncation occurs at the Nginx layer.
Config changes that reduce resource limits must be tested against the maximum payload sizes before deploying.
Session 7 note: the frontend team optimized the bulk export download to use a streaming response.
Old Ansible config: the proxy_buffer_size was set to 16MB in the original template.
The content-type for bulk export responses is application/octet-stream.
